question: In which year was the European Union established?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1993**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The European Union (EU) was formally established with the signing of the Maastricht Treaty on November 1, **1993**.
 
• The EU is a political and economic union of member countries that are located primarily in Europe.
 
• The Maastricht Treaty marked a significant milestone in the process of European integration, introducing new forms of cooperation between the member states' governments in areas such as defense, justice, and home affairs.
 
• The treaty also established the three pillars of the European Union: the European Communities, the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), and the Justice and Home Affairs (JHA).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The EU has its origins in the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) and the European Economic Community (EEC), formed by six countries in 1951 and 1958, respectively.
 
• The Maastricht Treaty also laid the groundwork for the creation of the euro, the EU's single currency, which was introduced in 1999 and came into physical circulation in 2002.
 
• The EU operates through a hybrid system of supranational and intergovernmental decision-making and has its own institutions, such as the European Commission, the European Parliament, and the European Court of Justice.
 
• As of now, the EU has 27 member countries, following the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the union in 2020, commonly known as Brexit.
